answer: Give each applicant one berth at a wharf and one radio beacon sealed in a pearl capsule that resonates at a frequency no second capsule shares. The beacon hops channels on a schedule keyed to its capsule; three posts around the wharf triangulate each hop's signal, and only a matching triangulation releases the next hop, so no signal can be faked from another berth. Halfway, a pearl check asks the beacon to answer a nonce with its resonance. One beacon costs $460 plus 24 installer hours; 5,000 fakes need 5,000 berths, $2.3 million and 120,000 hours, and no bulk order reserves a second berth.
